overview.description: Nine-Card Golf is a draw-and-discard shedding game played with a 3Ã—3 grid layout where players strategically replace cards to minimize their total score. A unique feature is the ability to score zero by collecting three cards of equal rank in a vertical column, adding a distinctive puzzle element to the Golf family.
overview.deck: One or two standard 52-card decks (depending on player count)

history.origins: Nine-Card Golf evolved from the classic Golf family of card games, which emerged in North America in the mid-20th century. The 3Ã—3 grid variant represents an expansion of six-card Golf, introducing more strategic depth through additional card combinations.
timeline: 1950s-1960s: Classic Golf variants (Six-Card, Four-Card) became popular in casual American gaming circles.
1970s: Nine-Card variant (Crazy Nines) emerged as an enhanced version with increased complexity and play time.
Present: Known as both 'Nine-Card Golf' and 'Crazy Nines'; remains a family favorite for group play.
history.evolution: The progression from Six-Card to Nine-Card Golf reflects the gradual increase in game complexity within the family. Nine-Card Golf adds strategic depth by increasing the grid size and introducing three-of-a-kind column bonuses.
history.cultural: Remains popular in casual family gaming and among card game enthusiasts who appreciate grid-based solitaire mechanics adapted for multiplayer competition.

setup.deck: One or two standard 52-card decks (one deck sufficient for 2-4 players; two decks for 5-8 players).
setup.equipment: Scorepad and pencils for tracking round scores.
setup.dealing: Dealer distributes nine cards face-down to each player, one at a time, in clockwise order. Each player arranges their cards in a 3Ã—3 grid (three rows of three cards). Before play begins, each player selects three of their nine cards to turn face-up; the remaining six stay face-down. The remaining deck is placed in the center as the stock, and the top card is flipped face-up beside it to start the discard pile.

rules.objective: Win the round by achieving the lowest total score when all nine cards in your grid are face-up.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Turn Sequence**: Players take turns in clockwise order, starting with the player to the dealer's left. 2. **Draw Phase**: On your turn, you must draw either the top card of the face-down stock OR the top card of the discard pile. 3. **Replacement Phase**: You must use the drawn card to replace exactly one card in your 3Ã—3 grid (if you drew from the discard pile, you cannot simply discard it again). Replace either a face-down card (revealing it) or a face-up card (which goes to the discard pile). 4. **Revealing**: If you replace a face-down card, it is now revealed to all players. 5. **End of Round**: The round ends immediately when one player has all nine cards face-up. That player does NOT take the remaining turns in that round.
keyRules: Grid Layout: Maintain a strict 3Ã—3 arrangement; cards cannot be rearranged after initial placement.
Face-Up Requirement: You must turn face-down cards face-up by replacing them.
Column Matching Bonus: Three cards of identical rank in the same vertical column score zero points (not horizontal or diagonal).
Discard Rule: If you take the top discard, you MUST use it to replace a card in your grid (cannot simply discard it).
No Card Rearrangement: Once cards are placed, you cannot move themâ€”only replace them.
End Condition: The round ends as soon as any player turns their final face-down card face-up.

strategy.basic: Early Game: Prioritize revealing your face-down cards quickly by drawing from the stock or strategically taking discards that allow useful replacements. Target high-value cards (face cards, aces if high) for replacement. Favor Kings since they score zero points.
strategy.intermediate: Column Control: Watch what cards have been revealed by opponents and in the discard pile. If you see two cards of the same rank, try to acquire the third to complete a zero-scoring column. Discard Management: Remember what's been played; avoid creating a discard pile full of cards that help opponents complete patterns. Position Awareness: Note which of your face-down cards are in the same column as high-value face-up cards, and prioritize replacing those face-down cards.
strategy.advanced: Endgame Prediction: As the round nears completion (when someone has 8-9 face-up cards), calculate which opponent will reveal their final card and when. Block them by refusing to replace certain high-value cards if it helps you more. Strategic Discard Timing: Sometimes hold onto low-value discards to prevent opponents from accessing cards they need. Calculate Opponent Columns: Deduce what face-down cards opponents likely hold based on their play pattern, and avoid giving them opportunities to complete three-of-a-kind columns.
tips: Early Reveals: Reveal high-point cards face-down early to avoid being surprised by high scores late in the round.
Three-of-a-Kind Hunt: If you've seen two cards of the same rank face-up (yours or discarded), immediately pursue the third card aggressively.
Kings are Gold: Always keep Kings if you draw them; they contribute zero points and can anchor your grid.
Endgame Math: Near the end, add up your current cards and estimate if you can win. Sometimes intentionally delaying revealing your last card is strategic if your score is high.
Discard Pile Reading: Pay close attention to the discard pile; it reveals which cards are in play and helps you predict future draws.

list.name: Two Cards Face-Up Start
list.description: Only two cards are revealed face-up at the start instead of three. This increases luck and decreases early-game certainty.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes initial reveal count only; engine constants could be extended to support this.

list.name: Four-Card Bonus
list.description: Four cards of identical rank in a 2Ã—2 square (any combination of rows/columns) score negative points (approximately -25). Three-of-a-kind columns still score zero.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring rule change would require engine support for 2x2 bonus and negative points.

list.name: Twos as Positive or Joker Rules
list.description: House variant: Twos score +2 instead of 2, or jokers (if added to deck) score -2 as wildcards.
list.emptyOverridesReason: House rules for twos and jokers need deck and scoring overrides when documented.

list.name: Extended Matching (Horizontal/Diagonal)
list.description: In addition to vertical columns, three-card rows (horizontal) or diagonals also score zero. This increases pattern complexity.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Pattern matching expansion would require engine support for row and diagonal zero-score.

list.name: Double-Deck Nine-Card Golf
list.description: For 6+ players, use two complete decks (104 cards) to ensure sufficient card variety and prevent running out of needed ranks.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Deck count override for 6+ players; engine.deckCount or constants could support this.

difficulty.easy: AI draws randomly from stock or discard with no strategic preference. Replaces cards randomly without considering column bonuses or score optimization.
difficulty.medium: AI evaluates immediate score impact of replacements. Attempts to create matching columns when two cards of the same rank are visible. Prefers drawing from discard when face-up cards are low-value.
difficulty.hard: AI tracks all revealed cards (both its own and opponents') to deduce probabilities of upcoming cards. Calculates which columns can be completed to maximize zero-scoring potential. Considers opponent grid states and strategic timing. Balances between aggressive column completion and defensive blocking of opponent patterns.

considerations: Grid Tracking: AI must maintain awareness of its own 3Ã—3 grid state and all opponents' partially revealed grids.
Column Completion Probability: Given known cards, calculate the likelihood of completing three-of-a-kind columns.
Discard Pile Analysis: AI must remember which cards have been discarded to inform draw decisions.
Endgame Detection: When opponents are close to revealing their final card, AI adjusts strategy to either finish the round favorably or block them.
Face-Down Card Inference: Based on remaining cards in deck and play patterns, estimate what face-down cards opponents likely hold.

engine.deckDescription: Standard 52-card deck comprising fifty-two cards: four suits of thirteen ranks each, with no jokers. One or two decks may be used depending on player count.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades), each with thirteen cards. Suits are equal in rank in this game.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit from Ace through King, Queen, Jack, down to 2. Cards have point values for scoring the grid.
engine.dealPattern: 9 cards per player in 3Ã—3 grid; 3 revealed face-up initially

synthesis.shortDescription: A draw-and-discard grid game where players strategically replace cards in a 3Ã—3 layout to minimize score. Special bonuses reward vertical three-card matches, adding puzzle-like depth to the classic Golf family.

prompts.human: Welcome to Nine-Card Golf, where you manage a 3Ã—3 grid of cards. Draw from the stock or discard pile each turn, then replace one card in your grid to reveal hidden cards. Achieve the lowest score by strategically creating zero-point column matches (three identical cards stacked vertically). Be first to reveal all your cardsâ€”or last, if your score is low enough to win!
prompts.ai: Game: Nine-Card Golf (Crazy Nines). Setup: Each player receives 9 cards arranged in a 3Ã—3 grid; 3 cards are revealed face-up initially. Gameplay: Draw stock or discard; use the card to replace one grid card (face-down cards are revealed when replaced). Scoring: Aces=1, 2-10=face value, J/Q=10, K=0. Three identical cards in a vertical column=0 (instead of their combined value). End: Round ends when any player reveals their final face-down card. Lowest score wins that round. Play multiple rounds; lowest cumulative score wins the game.

scoring.description: Players sum the point values of their nine cards. Lower scores are better. Certain combinations score zero.
scoring.winCondition: The player with the lowest total score at the end of a round wins that round. Multiple rounds are played, and the player with the lowest cumulative score across all rounds wins the game.
scoring.splitRules: No pot splitting; purely score-based. The player with the lowest grand total after multiple rounds is the overall winner.

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target score; play by game rules.
